findings.claim: An all-clients map-roles (or configure + map-roles-composite) grant also covers the realm-management client. An admin who also has map-roles on users can therefore give themselves or another user realm-management/realm-admin.
findings.evidence: RolePermissions.canMapRole (:308) and canMapComposite (:398) return true when root.clients().canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles(container) is true, which skips checkAdminRoles(role). ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(client,...) (:214-221) falls back to the all-clients resource for any client that has no resource of its own, and nothing excludes system clients. ClientRoleMappingsResource.addClientRoleMapping (:166-176) checks only users().requireMapRoles and roles().requireMapRole. In V1 this needed an explicit grant on realm-management. checkAdminRoles also compares against getRealmPermissionsClient(), which MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides. Reasoned; neither seat ran a test. Test sketch: all-clients MAP_ROLES + users MAP_ROLES for myadmin, then myadmin adds realm-admin to itself. Expected 403, predicted success.
findings.reason: Privilege escalation that two correctness seats reached independently, with source citations. Not rejected. Severity kept at the seats' Important; it may warrant Critical once confirmed by a test.

findings.claim: Realms whose admin-permissions client existed before this change never get the Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). getResourceTypeResource then returns null, findByResource(server, null) throws an NPE, and the caller gets HTTP 500 instead of 403. Creating a Clients permission fails with 'Scope [configure] does not exist'.
findings.evidence: AdminPermissionsSchema.init (:222-228) returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. RealmManager import (:567-570) also skips init. JPAPolicyStore.findByResource (:215) dereferences resource.getId() unconditionally. The patch adds no migration. hasPermission(String) (:244-247) null-guards; hasPermission(ClientModel,...) does not. The same NPE occurs when realm admin permissions are switched off after the client was created. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Three seats with source citations. Smallest fix: a null guard. A migration or idempotent init is needed for full coverage; the feature is EXPERIMENTAL (Profile.java:58).

findings.claim: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. Before this patch, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returned the V1 ClientPermissions, which returned false. With features token-exchange and admin-fine-grained-authz:v2 both on, a token exchange to another client's audience now gives HTTP 500 instead of 403.
findings.evidence: AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 calls AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...). management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is on. TOKEN_EXCHANGE has no dependency on FGAP V1 (Profile.java:76), so the combination is allowed. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Regression from false to an exception on a reachable path. OCR rated it Minor; the ledger takes the higher correctness rating. Smallest fix: return false.

findings.claim: canView() accepts only VIEW (or the default role), not MANAGE. An admin with only all-clients MANAGE therefore gets 403 on GET /client-scopes, every /client-scopes/{id} sub-resource and clientInitialAccess list. This contradicts canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel), which both accept MANAGE in the same patch.
findings.evidence: canListClientScopes (inherited) = canView() || QUERY_CLIENTS. ClientScopesResource.java:91 and :141 call requireListClientScopes(). ClientInitialAccessResource list() calls requireView(). The canView() Javadoc says VIEW only, while canView(ClientScopeModel) counts MANAGE. Reasoned. Test sketch: in testManageAllClients, call clientScopes().findAll(); predicted ForbiddenException.
findings.reason: The patch contradicts itself on whether MANAGE implies VIEW. One correctness seat, with source citations.

findings.claim: Once a per-client permission exists for client X, only X's own resource is evaluated, so all-clients permissions stop applying to X. Example: admin A has all-clients MANAGE; adding a VIEW-only permission on X for admin B removes A's manage on X.
findings.evidence: getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources without a type. DefaultPolicyEvaluator (:70-81) adds type-level policies only when resource.getType() != null. UserPermissionsV2 has the same pattern. No test combines an all-clients grant with a per-client grant on the same client. Reasoned.
findings.reason: OCR rated it Important, SP Minor. The behaviour is inherited from the existing Users resource-type semantics (UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission), so the root cause is in the shared evaluator and resource-type design, not this patch. Check that would settle it: an integration test granting all-clients MANAGE to A and per-client VIEW on myclient to B, then A updates myclient. ponytail: inherited semantics; fix in DefaultPolicyEvaluator/AdminPermissionsSchema for Users and Clients together.

findings.claim: The whole role/client/group removal listener is now gated on the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. With FGAP off entirely, leftover V1 permission data is no longer cleaned up on delete. Under V2, deleting a client leaves its per-client resource and the permissions that reference it orphaned.
findings.evidence: At base (b7b84d75d1, AdminPermissions.java:74-93) the listener had no gate. V1 and V2 are versions of the same feature (Profile.java:56/58). ClientApplicationSynchronizer has no V2 cleanup. Correctness seats note that some gate is needed, because ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws (:193).
findings.reason: Correctness seats rated it Minor, the spec seat Important. The ledger takes Important because base behaviour changes for every non-V1 deployment. Narrower fix: gate on !ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, or gate only the client branch under V2. V2 orphan cleanup may be deferred as a follow-up.

findings.claim: getClientsWithPermission never returns client IDs. findByType(server,'Clients') matches only the typed all-clients resource, so the result is {} or {'Clients'}. The caller AvailableRoleMappingResource:229-230 would NPE on realm.getClientById('Clients').
findings.evidence: Per-client resources come from resourceStore.create(...) without setType (AdminPermissionsSchema ~:102). The caller is reachable only under V1 (!isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)), and V1 and V2 are mutually exclusive (Profile.java:285).
findings.reason: Unreachable today. ponytail: latent wrong contract; fix when a V2 caller is added. Settling check: a unit or integration call of getClientsWithPermission with a per-client grant.

findings.claim: Dead code: private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken), the logger field, the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import, and the Scope, ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports are unused. They were copied from V1 token-exchange code that V2 does not support.
findings.evidence: Seat grep: getEvaluationContext, logger and TOKEN_EXCHANGE each occur only at their declaration (:46, :51, :262-272).
findings.reason: All four seats agree; deleting it does not change behaviour. Ponytail's Important was normalised to Minor.

findings.claim: The Javadoc on the void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says 'Returns true if...'. Both methods throw ForbiddenException.
findings.evidence: Method signatures are void (:95-103). The other require* docs in the same hunk say 'Throws ForbiddenException'.
findings.reason: Documentation is wrong; trivial fix.

findings.claim: The new 'For V2 only: Also if ... for all clients' Javadoc misdescribes V2. For the canMap* methods, V2 replaces the V1 per-client check rather than adding to it, and V2 also honours per-client grants.
findings.evidence: ClientPermissionsV2.java:91-103 use hasPermission alone. testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient and testManageOnlyOneClient depend on per-client grants.
findings.reason: Documentation contradicts the implementation.

findings.claim: The evaluate-and-match-scope loop is written three times. hasGrantedPermission (:274-286) duplicates the parent's private ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource,String) (:689). The two hasPermission overloads could be one varargs method with null meaning all clients, as UserPermissionsV2 does.
findings.evidence: Read from the code: ClientPermissions.java:689; UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(UserModel, EvaluationContext, String...).
findings.reason: Refactor with no behaviour change. Advisory. ponytail: consolidate when the scope-matching fixes (null guard, resourceId check) land, so they are written once.

findings.claim: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) does not filter on permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.java:135. Clients and Users evaluate differently, with no explanation.
findings.evidence: UserPermissionsV2.java:135 compared with ClientPermissionsV2.java:207-235.
findings.reason: No failing case shown: policies are already fetched by resource, so the outcome may be the same. ponytail: align when consolidating hasPermission. Settling check: a test with both a per-client and an all-clients permission evaluated for one client.

findings.claim: Re-implements helpers that already exist: hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) is canManageClientsDefault(), hasOneAdminRole(VIEW_CLIENTS, MANAGE_CLIENTS) at :119 is canViewClientDefault(), and canManageClientScopes() (:106-110) has the same body as canManage().
findings.evidence: Parent helpers exist in ClientPermissions. :86 already uses canViewClientDefault().
findings.reason: Trivial reuse with no behaviour change.

findings.claim: Test helpers became static and take (realm, client) arguments that the base class already holds. This caused about 40 call-site edits, and the new createPermission overloads at :163/:167 are instance methods, so the class is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Every caller passes the inherited realm and client fields (L48-52).
findings.reason: Style preference with no behaviour impact, and no documented standard requires either form. Reverting now would add more churn than it removes. Advisory seat.

findings.claim: createClientPolicy is never used.
findings.evidence: Seat grep across the fgap tests finds only the declaration.
findings.reason: Dead test helper; delete it.

findings.claim: Unrelated reformatting: the new gate re-indents the listener body, and the cast spacing changes from (X)event to (X) event. CONTRIBUTING.md says not to format code unrelated to the change.
findings.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'Do not format or refactor code that is not directly related to your contribution.' An early return would make the diff one line.
findings.reason: Breaches a documented standard. Addressed together with the listener-gate fix.

findings.claim: An empty line was replaced by a line of four spaces (trailing whitespace).
findings.evidence: Diff hunk at :53. CONTRIBUTING.md bans unrelated formatting.
findings.reason: Trivial.

findings.claim: The new private ClientPermissionsV2 clientPermissions field hides the inherited protected clientPermissions (MgmtPermissions.java:76).
findings.evidence: MgmtPermissions.java:76.
findings.reason: Copies the existing userPermissions pattern in the same class. ponytail: fix both shadowed fields together.

findings.claim: getResourceName handles only the Users type, so Clients resources (all-clients and per-client) have a null display name in permission representations.
findings.evidence: getResourceName falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which getOrCreateResource never sets. Seen in PolicyResourceService.java:218.
findings.reason: Schema extension incomplete; the name is visible in the admin API or UI.

findings.claim: Uses the JUnit 4 import static org.junit.Assert.fail. The same file otherwise uses JUnit 5 Assertions.
findings.evidence: tests/MIGRATING_TESTS.md:24,31 and docs/tests-development.md:29 say to avoid org.junit.Assert.*.
findings.reason: Breaches a documented standard.

findings.claim: Test isolation and coverage gaps. @AfterEach removes only permissions. testManageOnlyOneClient renames myclient and changes client-scope types, and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient (:326-334) leaves roles and mappings behind, so results depend on test order. testViewAllClients calls create(null), so it never tests a real payload. Nothing tests MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the client-scope endpoints, the realm-management escalation or V2 delete cleanup.
findings.evidence: Read from the test source. The realm is shared across tests.
findings.reason: Order-dependent tests are a real flakiness risk. Coverage for the escalation, NPE and canView findings comes with their red tests.

findings.claim: hasPermission(String) runs a full policy evaluation of the all-clients resource on every call without first checking whether any policies exist. canView(c) can trigger up to 4 evaluations per client. In GET /clients, when canView() is false, this runs over the whole unpaginated client list.
findings.evidence: Compared with the per-client variant and UserPermissionsV2, which short-circuit on empty policies. Reasoned; not measured.
findings.reason: Unmeasured performance claim. ponytail: add the empty-policies short-circuit when consolidating hasPermission. Settling check: time GET /clients in a realm with many clients as a query-users admin.

findings.claim: The patch adds no documentation for the Clients resource type or its scopes, while CONTRIBUTING.md says to include documentation.
findings.evidence: No V2 docs exist for the existing Users type either; the only hit is the V1 fine-grain.adoc.
findings.reason: Matches existing project practice for this EXPERIMENTAL feature, and the seat did not press it. ponytail: document Users and Clients together when V2 leaves experimental.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode): no build, tests, linters or type checker, so every finding is reasoned from source and none has executed evidence. Spec axis: no spec; checked only against the PR title's stated intent. Standards docs used: CONTRIBUTING.md, PR-CHECKLIST.md, docs/tests-development.md, tests/MIGRATING_TESTS.md, .editorconfig. open-code-review:delegate-review skipped all 5 test files (AbstractPermissionTest, PermissionClientTest, PermissionRESTTest, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest, UserResourceTypePermissionTest) via OCR default_path filtering, so only one correctness seat (superpowers) reviewed the tests in full. superpowers and mattpocock reviewed PermissionRESTTest, UserResourceTypePermissionTest and UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest only lightly, as mechanical refactors; ponytail checked PermissionClientTest and UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest only for helper usage and dead code. Not checked by any seat: the JPA cache-layer store, admin-console UI, compilation. No cross-family reviewer was available, so all four seats are the same model family. No Critical/Important correctness finding was rejected, so no Rejections-rule verifier was dispatched. Untracked harness dotfiles in the worktree (.bashrc, .claude/, .mcp.json, etc.) are not part of the change and were excluded from the pinned patch. Fix rounds, red tests and rounds 2+ were not run (benchmark mode).
